title: introduce-ack-windowed-reassembly-and-delimiter-normalization-for-json-streams
author: Asha Mehta
description: Motivation: Users reported intermittent broken JSON objects in streaming responses when the client receives tightly packed SSE fragments mixed with heartbeats and large binary token payloads. This caused structured output parsers and downstream function-call consumers to drop events or produce partial JSON parse errors. This PR introduces a small protocol-level improvement and deterministic reassembly behavior without changing the external API. Summary of changes: 1) ACK-window reassembly: maintain a bounded, per-stream ack-window (configurable, default 64 events) that accepts out-of-order fragments tagged with a lightweight event-seq id and defers emission until either the sequence fills the window or an explicit ack/timeout occurs; this prevents blind coalescing of fragments across unrelated events. 2) Delimiter normalization: introduce a normalization pass that collapses mixed CR/LF, zero-width whitespace, and doubled SSE delimiters into canonical single-delimiter tokens before JSON extraction; this prevents accidental splits when clients re-chunk network buffers. 3) Function-call and tool-call boundary preservation: allocate a small sentinel escape header for multi-part function-call payloads so that nested structured outputs do not get merged across event boundaries during coalescing. 4) Heartbeat & backpressure interaction: heartbeat frames are now treated as soft-acks (advance window by a single slot without forcing emission) to avoid premature sequence flushes under low-throughput clients; backpressure signals from the runtime will fast-forward the window for stalled streams. 5) Tests & telemetry: add exhaustive unit and integration tests covering interleaved heartbeats, high-frequency tiny chunks (1-8 bytes), and multi-tool-call streams; emit new metrics sse.reassembly.window_fill and sse.reassembly.dropped_out_of_window for observability. Compatibility and rollout: changes are backwards-compatible at the API level; existing clients will see fewer partial-JSON errors and unchanged event ids; rollout is staged: feature gated, enabled by default on canary for two weeks, then ramped to 100% with a re-run of canary tests. See linked Linear items for evaluation criteria and regression thresholds. Implementation notes: the reassembler is implemented in a small state machine in src/sse/reassembly.go with a normalization pipeline in src/sse/frame_normalizer.go; kept hot-path allocations minimal and added object pooling for fragment buffers. Performance: microbenchmarks show <4% median token latency increase at 1ms sequence windows and 0% p99 regression for typical chat workloads; load tests with bursty tiny-chunk clients show 28% reduction in parsed-json errors. Rollback plan: feature flag can be toggled per-cluster and we can disable ack-windows per-customer if any compatibility issue is detected. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-5042 - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Canary run results attached - [x] Docs updated (streaming guide)

review_conversation: Ethan Zhou (review): Can we guarantee that the ack-window won't grow unbounded if a client halts?
Asha Mehta (author): We bound the window and use a configurable timeout to force-forward; added metrics for dropped fragments and fast-forward counts.
Liam O'Connor (review): The function-call escape header looks ok but will downstream OpenAI compatibility clients need a parser update?

Asha Mehta (author): No client changes required for standard flows; only custom low-level integrations that parsed raw stream bytes will need to accept the new header; added compatibility note to streaming.md.
Priya Kapoor (approve): Verified canary results and integration tests, approving.
release_notes: Fixes intermittent partial-JSON and structured-output corruption in SSE streaming by introducing ack-windowed reassembly and delimiter normalization; reduces parse errors for tiny-chunk and high-frequency streams; no API breaking changes.
